subject: triangle distribution, bounds, NUTS hanging, and Pinocchioization

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: triangle distribution, bounds, NUTS hanging, and Pinocchioization
parts:
The triangle distro works out of the box.

src/demo/triangle.stan
-------------------------
parameters {
double(-1.0,1.0) y;
}
model {
lp__ <- lp__ + log(1.0 - abs(y));
}
------------------------

This model draws a single sample from the "unit"
triangle density with support on (-1,1) and density

p(y) = 1 - abs(y).

The parameter is declared with the bounds as a
constraint. It uses the implicit variable "lp__"
to define the log probability function. (This
maneuver will let us sum out discrete variables.)

With the bounds in place, here are the quantiles
from 3 runs:

0% 25% 50% 75% 100%
-0.934 -0.318 -0.032 0.285 0.987

-0.983 -0.290 -0.026 0.315 0.971

-0.986 -0.303 0.003 0.283 0.931

The exact quantiles are (-1, -0.3, 0, 0.3, 1).

The density plot looks reasonably triangular too.

There seems to be an awful lot of rejection:

-0.123279
-0.24086
-0.24086
-0.24086
-0.24086
0.140527
0.140527
0.140527
-0.751579
-0.751579
-0.751579
-0.751579
0.87068
0.526088
0.746389
-0.636355
0.408008
0.408008
0.408008
0.408008

I'm wondering if this has anything to do with crossing
the undifferentiable point at zero.

Without the declared bounds on y, the current implementation
has problems. It doesn't get into the corners and the 50%
intervals don't look good.

0% 25% 50% 75% 100%
-0.805 -0.282 0.008 0.355 0.869

-0.892 -0.274 -0.017 0.267 0.856

-0.858 -0.273 0.007 0.338 0.885

-0.884 -0.315 -0.024 0.250 0.817

It can also hang during burn-in/adaptation (it hung
twice in 20 or so runs). This is probably fixable.

I believe this is what one of Andrew's friends
hypothesized would happen (I'd be happy to cite
him or her in the doc).

There are also problems even with a bounded y if
I use the reflected triangle density, also with
support on (-1,1):

p(y) = abs(y)

NUTS hangs in the burnin stage every time, even if
the initial value isn't zero. I rather expected
it to shoot past the undifferentiable point at zero.

At a future Stan meeting, I can talk about some
Pinocchioization opportunities arising from Stan's
parameterization of the unbounded case (aka, more
fun with Jacobians).

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] triangle distribution, bounds, NUTS hanging, and Pinocchioization
parts:
Nondifferentiability should cause problems, for sure. What might be
happening is the step size keeps decreasing without bound due to the
impossibility of accurate simulation. I'll have to take a closer look
at this sometime when I get back.

Matt
